title: SDK adopter playlist and anti-friction checklist
content:
Purpose:
A compact, tactical checklist + sequence of tiny wins ("playlist") to get new SDK adopters from zero -> sample app in under 10 minutes and to remove first-run friction. This doc is intentionally lightweight: a set of experiments, short scripts, and anti-friction patterns we can ship into docs, examples, and the CLI.

Scope:
- Public SDKs (Python, JS) and the CLI
- First-run UX: install, auth, simple generate, streaming, embeddings
- Entrypoints for Dedicated/Private customers (notes only)
- Telemetry & error contract minimal requirements

Desired outcomes (metrics to watch):
- time_to_first_success < 10m (measured by quickstart completion funnel)
- first_request_success_rate > 95%
- followup_sample_app_run_rate within 48h > 25%

Playlists (ordered tiny wins to present to users)
1) "Hello world" (30s)
   - install pip/npm
   - set REDWOOD_API_KEY env var
   - run a single generate call and print output
   - show where request appears in Console (link)
   Example (python):
   ```python
   from redwood import RedwoodClient
   c = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
   print(c.generate(text='Summarize: why Redwood?'))
   ```
   (Make this a single copy-paste block in docs)

2) Streaming demo (1–2m)
   - show client.stream() with progress to stdout
   - include fallback to non-streaming for environments without websockets

3) A one-file sample app (3–5m)
   - input box + model selector + streaming output
   - minimal dependencies, runnable with `python sample_app.py`
   - emphasize set of env vars for Dedicated vs Hosted

4) Embeddings quickcheck (1m)
   - generate embedding request to index two short docs and run cosine similarity

5) Error-recovery pattern (2m)
   - common transient: 429/503 -> exponential backoff + jitter + fallback to cheaper model
   - show concrete code snippets including detecting token-limit errors and truncation hints

Anti-friction checklist (items for docs/CLI/examples)
- single bash/curl example that works without SDK deps (curl + HTTP)
- single JS and Python example that are copy-paste runnable (no extra imports beyond SDK)
- example env var helper script (set-quickstart-env.sh) that swaps between hosted/dedicated/private endpoints
- clear message for auth failures: actionable next step (login link, test token generator)
- include one minimal streaming and one non-streaming example for environments like Codespaces
- short troubleshooting section embedded in quickstart (top 6 errors with fixes)

Telemetry & acceptance contract (minimal)
- Quickstart success event: sdk.quickstart.completed (fields: sdk_name, language, sample_id)
- Quickstart failure event: sdk.quickstart.error (fields: sdk_name, error_class, step)
- Instrument CLI with the same events but only when user opts in (privacy-first; CLI prompt)
- Telemetry must not log API keys or prompt text. Only hashed prompt_id or a prompt-length bucket

CLI suggestions (short):
- `redwood quickstart --lang python --sample 1` -> scaffold one-file app and optionally run it
- CLI should detect Windows/Codespaces and print platform-specific hints for streaming
- `redwood auth test` returns 200 + small payload showing account, usable regions, model list (useful for quick troubleshooting)

Docs surfaces to update (priority order)
- Quickstart landing page (single-screen flow with copy-paste)
- Examples repo: add `one-file-webhook-demo.py` + `embed-and-search.js`
- SDK README top-of-file: 3 copy-paste blocks (curl, python, js)
- Console: link to sample app with a built-in try-it runner (hosted)

Edge cases & error patterns (notes for SDK engineers)
- Token limit error: return structured error with fields {type: 'token_limit', allowed: 4096, attempted: 8200} (we need consistent shape across SDKs)
- Streaming partials: ensure resumed streams include a resume_token when reconnecting
- Local dev proxies: recommend `--insecure-local-proxy` for self-hosted with local cert issues but warn on security

Experiment ideas (A/B candidates)
- Inline quickstart vs guided CLI tour: which leads to more sample app runs?
- One-click repo generation (GitHub template) vs zip download: measure time-to-run
- Minimal telemetry opt-in prompt at CLI vs separate environment opt-in via UI

Sample troubleshooting (top 6 with fixes)
1) 401 / missing API key -> checklist: env var, `redwood auth test`, rate-limit messaging
2) 429 burst -> explain retry header hints and proposed backoff snippet
3) token limit -> show truncation snippet + how to switch to streaming for long outputs
4) embedding diffs -> normalization mismatch: recommend L2 norm + consistent dtype conversion in examples
5) websocket blocked in Codespaces -> fallback to polling stream
6) model mismatch between Console and SDK -> `redwood models list` to surface model variants and compatibility

Open questions / TODOs
- Should quickstart scaffold include unit tests? (pro: shows baseline assertions; con: extra friction)
- Which sample_id do we ship as default? (small chat vs summarizer vs embedder)
- How do we measure time_to_first_success reliably without invasive telemetry? Proposed: self-hosted quickstart-runner that emits an event upon user-run opt-in.

Next immediate actions (owners)
- Maya: draft single-file python sample app for `one-file sample` + add to examples repo (ETA 11/14)
- Samir: implement `redwood quickstart` CLI MVP that scaffolds and optionally runs (ETA 11/22)
- Lina: design quickstart landing copy and single-screen UX (ETA 11/18)
- Ethan: propose telemetry event schema in tracking board (ETA 11/20)

Notes to self / informal ideas (keep short):
- Favor code that "just works" over super-opinionated frameworks in quickstarts
- Use small models as defaults to keep cost and latency tiny for new users
- Add a one-click codepen/stackblitz for JS samples if friction is low

Links (internal) and anchors:
- onboarding-ux research doc: CONFLUENCE-1234
- sdk-tracking-ticket: JIRA-DE-4521
- examples repo PR: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/pull/78

Revision history:
- 2024-11-07 Maya: initial sketch
- 2024-11-18 Samir: added CLI surface notes
- 2024-12-02 Lina: updated checklist + telemetry notes

End of doc.
